how_read: scripts/kb/fetch_wiki_live_pages.py logic (page text as rendered by the wiki, link markup removed), asked by page title: the wiki answered HTTP 403 to the reader's render call by revision number tonight, so a small wrapper used the reader's own functions and asked for the render by page title, and checked the revision the wiki rendered equals the revision the reader resolved. Every quoted sentence below was checked, by script, to appear word for word (whitespace collapsed) in the page text read at the revision named. A table row is quoted as its cells joined by ' || ' (a description cell closes with a double quote). Several pages describe a recurring item or character across the whole series; a line states a Mario Party 6 fact only where the page says so for Mario Party 6.

lines.line: Summary: At night in Party Mode the Donkey Kong Spaces of the day turn into Bowser Spaces, and landing on one makes Bowser hold a mini-game or a Bowser Bonus that can cost you coins, Orbs or a Star.

quoted: Bowser Spaces appear only during the night in Party Mode, replaced by DK Spaces during the day.
Bowser takes the coins or Orbs of any player who loses.
Bowser now hits a special Dice Block in this event, displaying a certain number of coins or Stars. Bowser then steals the number of coins and Stars indicated from the player.
These replace DK Spaces during the night.

lines.line: Weak points: Win the Bowser mini-game: only the players who lose pay him, in coins or Orbs, and the winners keep theirs. Landing with no coins is harmless: he hands you 10 coins and runs neither a mini-game nor a Bonus.

quoted: He'll take either half or all of the losers' coins, or all of their Orbs while sparing the winners'.
Bowser takes the coins or Orbs of any player who loses.
If a player does not have any coins when landing on a Bowser Space, Bowser gives them 10 coins and does not start a Bowser minigame or Bowser Bonus.

lines.line: Tips: In the Bowser Bonus he strikes a special Dice Block that can land on 5, 10, 20 or 30 coins, or a Star, and whoever stopped there loses that amount. A Star result costs nothing if you hold no Star. Clockwork Castle has no Bowser Spaces.

quoted: The Bowser Bonus may also occur, allowing him to roll a Dice Block to steal either five, 10, 20, 30 coins or even a Star from the player that landed on the space.
Bowser then steals the number of coins and Stars indicated from the player.
If Bowser hits a Star and the player does not have any, Bowser does not steal anything.
There are no Bowser Spaces or DK Spaces in Clockwork Castle.

lines.line: Summary: By day, the Donkey Kong Spaces on a Party Mode board bring Donkey Kong in for an event: a mini-game where players trade bananas for coins, or a DK Bonus for the player who landed.

quoted: These spaces appear only during the day. Donkey Kong appears and causes an event, such as minigames where players can trade in bananas for coins. The DK Bonus may also occur, allowing the player to roll a DK Barrel to earn either five, 10, 20, 30 coins or even a Star.

lines.line: Looks like: A yellow-orange space showing Donkey Kong's face. No other game colours these spaces yellow-orange; elsewhere they are blue.

quoted: this is the only game where DK Spaces are yellow-orange instead of blue and the last one to use DK's face as the space's emblem.

lines.line: Tips: The DK Bonus here rolls a barrel-shaped Dice Block worth 5, 10, 20 or 30 coins, or a Star. Night swaps every DK Space for a Bowser Space. Clockwork Castle has none, because Donkey Kong and Bowser both turn up on that board.

quoted: they are only around during the day, as they are replaced with Bowser Spaces at night.
The DK Bonus now involves a Dice Block shaped like a barrel
There are no DK Spaces or Bowser Spaces in Clockwork Castle due to Donkey Kong and Bowser appearing on the board.
allowing the player to roll a DK Barrel to earn either five, 10, 20, 30 coins or even a Star.

lines.line: Summary: On Snowflake Lake, Chain Chomps live in the board's four doghouses, and a player who pays to ride one steals a Star from every rival it passes. Stars cannot be bought on this board.

quoted: Unlike other boards in the Mario Party series, players must win by stealing Stars from other players by riding Chain Chomps, found in the four doghouses throughout the board.
When a player reaches a doghouse, they can pay coins to ride a Chain Chomp.
Since this board lacks Star Spaces, there are no means of buying Stars.
The Chain Chomp steals Stars from any player it passes, unless that player has a Snack Orb.

lines.line: Weak points: A Snack Orb stops one Chain Chomp theft: you toss a bone, the Chomp leaps over your space to fetch it and keeps moving, and anyone sharing your space is spared as well. It works one time only. Team games have one catch: teammates share Orbs and cannot trap each other, yet a teammate's Chain Chomp ride can still burn through your Snack Orb.

quoted: the user throws a bone into the air, causing the opponent's Chain-Chomp to jump over the user's space to catch it and then continue moving.
every player on the same space as the user also does not get hit by Chain-Chomp.
Prevents a Chain Chomp from stealing from you one time. Can't be used or placed.
Teammates share Orbs, coins, Stars, and cannot be affected by each others traps; however, Chain Chomps in Snowflake Lake can still use up a teammate's Snack Orb, despite being on the same team.

lines.line: Looks like: A metal ball, black or deep blue, with wide round eyes and a huge mouth of razor-sharp teeth; many are bigger than Mario.

quoted: Chain Chomps resemble a black or dark blue ball, sometimes with chains attached to them.
Many descriptions state Chain Chomps are made out of steel, iron or simply metal.
They have big circular eyes, large gaping mouths, and razor-sharp teeth.
Chain Chomps appear in various sizes, often bigger than Mario.

lines.line: Tips: Everyone starts with 5 Stars, more when a Star handicap is set. A Chain Chomp rider flattens whoever it reaches, teammates included, and takes their Star. Riding costs coins, and the price at night differs from the daytime one.

quoted: Each player starts with 5 Stars (or more depending on the number of Star handicaps).
Chain Chomp riders that reach other players squish them, including teammates, and steal their Star.

During the daytime, a ride costs 20 coins, and the player determines the spaces they move with one Dice Block. At night, players can purchase up to three Dice Blocks per ride, with each one costing 10 coins.

lines.line: Summary: A pink Boo who steals for hire at night, found only on Towering Treetop and Castaway Bay. Pay 5 coins to have her take coins from a player, or 40 to have her take a Star.

quoted: Pink Boo offers anyone who passes by it to steal coins or a star for them during the night as well. Players pay 5 coins for Pink Boo to take coins and 40 coins for Pink Boo to take a star from a player.
This is the only board other than Towering Treetop to feature Pink Boo, who will give her services to someone who comes by as long as it is nighttime.
In Mario Party 6, a Pink Boo appears in Towering Treetop and Castaway Bay.

lines.line: Weak points: Holding a Boo-Away Orb blocks her theft from you once; it triggers automatically and cannot be used or placed. She works only at night.

quoted: Prevents a Boo from stealing from you one time. Can't be used or placed.
it now protects against Pink Boo instead of the ordinary Boo
as long as it is nighttime.
If it is nighttime, she offers to steal either a star or coins.

lines.line: Looks like: A pink Boo, sometimes a light red one.

quoted: are a pink-colored (or occasionally light red-colored) variant of Boo

lines.line: Tips: She does the ordinary Boo's old job here, since Boo has become a playable character. You can buy the Boo-Away Orb only on her two boards, at 10 coins.

quoted: as Pink Boo has replaced Boo's role in the game, with Boo instead being a playable character.
The Boo-Away Orb is obtainable only in Towering Treetop and Castaway Bay, as those are the only boards on which Pink Boo can be found.
Prevents a Boo from stealing from you one time. Can't be used or placed." || Towering Treetop and Castaway Bay || 10 coins

lines.line: Summary: At night the tree at the top of Towering Treetop is Evil Woody instead of Woody, and the ? Space beside him rains Spiny eggs that make every player lose coins, where Woody's daytime shower gives coins.

quoted: If it is day, the player sees Woody, who showers coins on all the spaces and players. If it is night, he is replaced with his counterpart, Evil Woody, who makes Spiny eggs rain down on all spaces and players, who lose coins during the shower.
Woody returns in Mario Party 6's Towering Treetop, where he can be seen at the top of the giant tree.
Whenever a character lands on one of Evil Woody's Event Spaces, instead of him giving coins as Woody does, Evil Woody instead takes away coins by dropping Spinies on every character.

lines.line: Looks like: A tree whose face always looks angry, coloured blue with purple leaves, which is Woody's palette turned around.

quoted: Evil Woody has a perpetually angry expression and a hostile attitude. His color palette is also an inversion of Woody's color palette, being blue with purple leaves.

lines.line: Tips: Day gives way to night every three turns. A meter at the start of each turn counts the turns left, which helps you pick when to step on that space. At night the Spiny shower hits every player, not only the one who landed, while by day the same space gives coins to all.

quoted: Indicated by a meter by the beginning of every turn and by the pause menu, players can see how many turns the day time has left.
After the third time, day changes to night, which also lasts three turns.
If the Happening Space next to him is landed on, he gives coins to everyone, but only during the day, as he is replaced by Evil Woody at night.
The ? Space at the top of the board has two functions, depending on what time of day it is.
If it is day, the player sees Woody, who showers coins on all the spaces and players.
Evil Woody instead takes away coins by dropping Spinies on every character.

lines.line: Summary: Mario Party 6 has two Whomps that block a path: one on Snowflake Lake, one on Faire Square. Each charges 10 coins to let you pass.

quoted: Two Whomps have a role of blocking a path on a board in Mario Party 6, appearing in Snowflake Lake and Faire Square, respectively. Both Whomps charge the player ten coins to pass.

lines.line: Looks like: A big stone slab shaped like a rectangle, with a permanent scowl, glowing red eyes, five crooked teeth in an open mouth, plain arms and feet without legs.

quoted: They are large enemies that resemble rectangular stone slabs with snaggletoothed faces, simple hands and arms, and legless feet.
Like Thwomps, they have red eyes, though Whomps' appear to be glowing over black sclera. Their faces feature permanently angry expression and open mouth with five misaligned teeth.

lines.line: Tips: On Snowflake Lake the Whomp stands just before an Orb Shop, and getting past him leaves you on the right of the frozen pond. On Faire Square he blocks a path through the board's centre; paying lets you hop back to Brighton or Twila fast for another shot at Stars, which can save turns.

quoted: A Whomp blocks a path in front of an Orb Shop and charges 10 coins for people to pass. Going this way will take the player to the right side of the frozen pond.
Other events include a Whomp that blocks a path in the middle of the board.
but allows players to quickly revisit Brighton or Twila for another opportunity to receive more Stars, which can save precious turns.

lines.line: Summary: Snowflake Lake's nights bring big Freezies that close off the routes toward the board's centre; they thaw once daylight returns.

quoted: Also, during the night, large Freezies appear, blocking the paths to the middle of the board. They will melt when daylight comes.
In Mario Party 6, during the night at Snowflake Lake, Freezies block players from accessing other paths.

lines.line: Weak points: Daylight melts them, so head for the centre during the day, when nothing blocks the routes.

quoted: Also, during the night, large Freezies appear, blocking the paths to the middle of the board. They will melt when daylight comes.

lines.line: Looks like: A big figure formed wholly from ice, wearing a puzzled look.

quoted: is an enemy made entirely of ice
but each has a distinct puzzled expression.
large Freezies appear

lines.line: Tips: The time of day flips every three turns, and the pause menu tells you how many remain until the next flip. Stepping on a ? Space beside the frozen pond starts a coin game; at night it is a snowball fight in which players knock coins loose from one another.

quoted: players can view how many turns there are left, what time of the day it is and how many turns it will take to change the time of the day.
After the third time, day changes to night, which also lasts three turns.
Landing on a ? Space next to the frozen pond activates a coin game.
At night, players throw snowballs at each other to knock coins out of them for the taking.

lines.line: Summary: The reverse of a Star Space: stopping here saddles you with a Shadow Star, taking a Star from you, or coins when you hold none. In this game only two boards use it: Castaway Bay and Clockwork Castle.

quoted: The opposite of Star Spaces, these give the player a Shadow Star, which takes away a Star, or coins if the player has none. They appear only in Castaway Bay and Clockwork Castle and do not count toward the total.

lines.line: Weak points: On Castaway Bay the Shadow Star comes from Bowser on his Battle Yacht. Anyone stopping on DK's Riverboat makes the two boats trade places, so look at where each boat sits before you land.

quoted: Whenever someone stops on DK’s Riverboat, it’ll swap places with Bowser’s Battle Yacht!
makes players hit a circular target on the pole, making a bell sound that switches Bowser's and DK's boats around.

lines.line: Tips: On Castaway Bay a player with no Star pays 20 coins instead. On Clockwork Castle a Warp Pipe is the way to get clear of Bowser.

quoted: players that stop at Bowser's Battle Yacht will meet up with Bowser, who gives them a Shadow Star that takes away a star (or 20 coins if they do not have a star).
If you need to escape from Bowser or catch DK, don't hesitate to hop into a Warp Pipe.

lines.line: Summary: A green Orb that only works on yourself: a Bullet Bill carries you past a rival and you pocket 20 coins from them.

quoted: Catch a ride on a Bullet Bill and overtake an opponent to steal 20 coins.
All of these orbs affect the player or the Dice Block when the player uses them.
players can use a Bullet Bill Orb only on themselves

lines.line: Uses: Fly past an opponent to take 20 coins from them. It also carries you over roadblocks without setting them off. On Faire Square, where rivals bunch up in the middle of the board, it can hit them for a lot of coins.

quoted: it also allows players to pass roadblocks without triggering them.
As players congregate in the center zone, players with the Bullet Bill Orb can target them for significant coins.
Catch a ride on a Bullet Bill and overtake an opponent to steal 20 coins.

lines.line: Tips: Only E. Gadd's Garage and Faire Square sell it. An Orb hut charges 20 coins, or 10 in a flash sale. Use it close to the Star Space and you sail past the Star, so hold it back when you mean to buy one.

quoted: Catch a ride on a Bullet Bill and overtake an opponent to steal 20 coins." || E. Gadd's Garage and Faire Square || 20 coins
it costs 20 coins, or 10 during a flash sale, at an Orb hut
Using a Bullet Bill Orb near the Star Space causes players to fly past it.

lines.line: Summary: A green Orb that calls in Flutter, who carries you directly to the Star Space.

quoted: Flutter will appear and fly you straight to the Star Space!

lines.line: Uses: Only you can be its target. Towering Treetop and E. Gadd's Garage, the boards that sell it, put the Star somewhere new once it has been bought.

quoted: players can use a Flutter Orb only on themselves.
Flutter will appear and fly you straight to the Star Space!" || Towering Treetop and E. Gadd's Garage || 30 coins
A board where the star appears in a random spot, costing twenty coins to purchase, then moves to a different location.
Stars are obtained the same way as in Towering Treetop.
The Star will move to a different location as soon as someone grabs it.

lines.line: Tips: An Orb hut sells it for 30 coins. A Star costs 20 coins on Towering Treetop and on E. Gadd's Garage.

quoted: It costs 30 coins at an Orb hut.
On this board, Stars cost 20 coins.
Rush to the Star Space with 20 coins to buy a Star.

lines.line: Summary: A green Orb that turns the player who uses it into metal.

quoted: A Metal Mushroom Orb has the effect of turning the user metal

lines.line: Uses: Use it before you cross spaces where rivals left trap Orbs. Metal beats most of them: a Thwomp bounces off, a Tweester fizzles out, a Podoboo's fire does nothing, you kick a Bob-omb aside, a Koopa Troopa cannot carry something so heavy and quits, and a Zap Orb's Amps vanish after a failed zap.

quoted: the Thwomp will attempt to crush that player, but it will be deflected, negating the roadblock.
the Tweester still tries to blow away that player, but it dissipates shortly after with no effect.
The attack is negated if that player is under the effect of a Metal Mushroom Orb.
if the player is under the effect of a Metal Mushroom Orb, they simply kick away the Bob-omb.
Paratroopa will try to lift the player, but it gives up after a while, saying that the player is too heavy to lift.
the Amps will try to shock them, but they disappear after that.

lines.line: Tips: Every board has it except Towering Treetop and Faire Square, and the board pages say that makes roadblocks there especially tough to dodge.

quoted: The Metal Mushroom Orb does not spawn on this board, making Roadblocks placed on there particularly difficult to avoid.
The lack of Metal Mushroom Orbs available in the board makes Roadblocks difficult to avoid
this orb can be obtained on all boards except Towering Treetop and Faire Square

lines.line: Summary: A red Orb that goes on a space and acts as a roadblock. An opponent passing over gets squashed by a Thwomp and their move ends there.

quoted: Any opponent who passes it will get Thwomped and must stop moving.
players can only place it on a space as a roadblock.
Opponents that pass a space containing the Orb get flattened by a Thwomp, ending their turn.

lines.line: Uses: Leave it on a space your rivals have to cross. On Faire Square it can keep a player from buying Stars, most of all at night when Stars may be cheaper, and players often place it on the Red Space just ahead of the fixed Star space.

quoted: The Thwomp Orb, for instance, can prevent a player from obtaining Stars especially at night if it is cheaper than in day.
It is often placed at the Red Space right before the fixed Star space

lines.line: Tips: An Orb hut sells it for 10 coins, 5 during a flash sale, and the boards that stock it are Towering Treetop, Faire Square and Clockwork Castle. A rival under a Metal Mushroom Orb walks through unharmed, and you cannot put a new roadblock on top of one until an opponent has set it off.

quoted: It costs ten coins or five during a flash sale at the Orb Shop.
If a player is under the effect of the Metal Mushroom Orb, the Thwomp will attempt to crush that player, but it will be deflected, negating the roadblock.
Any opponent who passes it will get Thwomped and must stop moving." || Towering Treetop, Faire Square, and Clockwork Castle || 10 coins
they cannot be replaced until an opponent triggers the effect

lines.line: Summary: A yellow Orb that can only be placed on a space. A Piranha Plant bites a rival who stops there, and that rival hands you half their coins.

quoted: Any opponent who lands on it must give you half of their coins.
it becomes the Piranha Plant Orb that players can only place on a space
Opponents that land on a space containing the Orb are still eaten by a Piranha Plant and lose half their coins, which are then transferred to the space's owner.

lines.line: Uses: Put it where rivals tend to stop. Landing on your own Orb gives you 5 coins. If you are already on the space when a rival lands, the plant goes for the rival alone.

quoted: If the owner lands on the space, they receive five coins.
If a player is already on the space of this orb, and another opponent lands on it, the Piranha Plant chews only the opponent, while the original player gets surprised.

lines.line: Tips: It costs 15 coins, and every board sells it apart from Towering Treetop and Castaway Bay. It reacts to anyone who stops on the space, and remains until another Orb replaces it or a Star Space turns up on that square.

quoted: Any opponent who lands on it must give you half of their coins." || All boards except Towering Treetop and Castaway Bay || 15 coins
These orbs have an effect on a player who lands on the space.
The orb also stays on the board as long as no one replaces the orb or if a Star Space does not appear on it.
it costs fifteen coins at the Orb Shop.

lines.line: Summary: A blue Orb found only on Snowflake Lake; it shields you against one Chain Chomp theft.

quoted: Prevents a Chain Chomp from stealing from you one time. Can't be used or placed." || Snowflake Lake || 10 coins
It is only found on Snowflake Lake

lines.line: Uses: Just carry one around; it cannot be used or placed. The first time a rival's Chain Chomp comes for you, it triggers by itself: you toss a bone, the Chomp hops over your space to fetch it, and anybody else standing there is spared as well. You can discard the Orb at any time. On a team, even a teammate's Chain Chomp ride can burn your Snack Orb.

quoted: They cannot be thrown on a space or used. Instead, they are used automatically. They can be disposed at any time if the players chooses to, though.
Teammates share Orbs, coins, Stars, and cannot be affected by each others traps; however, Chain Chomps in Snowflake Lake can still use up a teammate's Snack Orb, despite being on the same team.
the user throws a bone into the air, causing the opponent's Chain-Chomp to jump over the user's space to catch it and then continue moving.
every player on the same space as the user also does not get hit by Chain-Chomp.

lines.line: Tips: An Orb hut charges 10 coins, and one Orb covers a single theft, so buy a fresh one after it is spent.

quoted: Prevents a Chain Chomp from stealing from you one time. Can't be used or placed." || Snowflake Lake || 10 coins

lines.line: Summary: A blue Orb that blocks one theft by Pink Boo; you cannot use it or place it.

quoted: Prevents a Boo from stealing from you one time. Can't be used or placed.
it now protects against Pink Boo instead of the ordinary Boo

lines.line: Uses: Keep one in hand on Towering Treetop or Castaway Bay and it fires on its own when a rival pays Pink Boo to come after you. It is the Gaddlight from earlier games, a flashlight whose beam frightens Boo off. You may discard the Orb whenever you want.

quoted: They cannot be thrown on a space or used. Instead, they are used automatically. They can be disposed at any time if the players chooses to, though.
The Gaddlight reappears in Mario Party 6, now in Orb form as the Boo-Away Orb.
It is a flashlight that can be used to prevent Boo from stealing from its holder
flashing the Boo with the item's light to scare it away.
The Boo-Away Orb retains the Gaddlight's effects from Mario Party 4

lines.line: Tips: An Orb hut charges 10 coins. Only the two boards that have Pink Boo, Towering Treetop and Castaway Bay, stock it.

quoted: Prevents a Boo from stealing from you one time. Can't be used or placed." || Towering Treetop and Castaway Bay || 10 coins
The Boo-Away Orb is obtainable only in Towering Treetop and Castaway Bay, as those are the only boards on which Pink Boo can be found.
